contract_grounding.note: violates=true is the honest literal reading: the observed 200 body contains five of the six listed members and the resharding_operations key is absent (not null, not empty list), and the observed field is inside the quote's domain — so either the value is non-compliant with the quoted claim (chosen) or a different constraint would have to be cited; there is no third reading. Dispatch nuance: candidates.jsonl carried constraint_id="" for this defect_id; the constraint is recovered verbatim from structured_contract.json type_constraints, and the script header (debate_logs/state_cluster_collection_info_002.py line 6 'constraint_ids: qdrant_type_cluster_collection_info_001') and chunks.json unit mapping (chunk_cluster+collection+info) confirm the binding — an extraction artifact, not a missing constraint. Mitigating facts for the auditor (do not weaken the literal violation): (a) v1.18.x OpenAPI itself lists resharding_operations as optional/nullable, required only in <=v1.11.x, so the assertion overstates the version's own schema; (b) source marks the omission deliberate (see source_grounding); (c) the script's state/count reconciliations all passed — the defect rests solely on the response-shape face.

Comparative face (source-level; live gRPC probe unavailable in this REST-only sandbox — face_unavailable for live probes, recorded from source): the gRPC face collections.proto:966 declares 'repeated ReshardingInfo resharding_operations = 6' and conversions.rs:1559-1563 flattens None into an empty repeated field, so gRPC always carries the member while REST omits it — a deliberate face-level divergence in how the same info is surfaced.

mundane_explanation.surviving: by_design: the omission is a deliberate serde skip with explicit maintainer intent evidence — types.rs:340 comment 'TODO(resharding): remove this skip when releasing resharding' above skip_serializing_if, plus upstream integration tests asserting absence in the idle case (test_resharding_extras.py:63,154,225); additionally the v1.18.x OpenAPI itself dropped the field from required (optional, nullable:true) vs v1.11.x. The residual question for the auditor is documentation/contract strictness (the published example still shows the member, and the extractor's assertion made it unconditional), not unintended server behavior.
